---
title: "Part 2 — Composing Sandcastles with Crossplane"
---

Part 2 will develop how the Crossplane composition layer *requests*
engineering work from the Sandcastle construction layer. The intended
learning arc is:

- A learner authors a Crossplane Composite Resource asking for a
  new Open Engineering artifact (for example, a new Pico kind).
- The Composition turns that request into an **EngineeringTask**
  (or equivalent) — a declarative record of the construction work
  the cluster wants done.
- A Sandcastle picks up the EngineeringTask, spins up an isolated
  workspace with the right tools and permissions, runs an
  engineering agent through the [Part 1 agent inner loop](../part-1/01-inside-a-sandcastle/index.qmd),
  and returns durable Git artifacts.
- Crossplane then reconciles those artifacts back onto the cluster,
  closing the compose → construct → behave loop.

## Lessons

- [01 Composing a Sandcastle request](01-composing-a-sandcastle-request/index.qmd)
  — the first Part 2 lesson. Covers the compose → construct
  boundary: how a Crossplane XR becomes an **EngineeringTask**, how
  a Sandcastle consumes the task (never the XR), and how the
  construction stage stays parametric on the request. Runnable
  end-to-end via the reusable
  [Compose a Sandcastle request lab](../../../labs/compose-sandcastle-request/).

::: {.callout-note title="Status — Part 2 lesson 01 runnable; further lessons scaffolded"}
